title: A negative-binomial model raised fixed-mean count log scores after 323 shallow M6.5+ earthquakes in 2013-2024
abstract: We tested whether a training-only count variance correction improves probability scores without a change to the mean. We used a fixed ComCat snapshot, 363 training centers in 2001-2012 and 323 test centers in 2013-2024. Centers have M6.5 or more and depth at most 70 km. Targets are M5.5+ neighbor counts on days 7-30 within 200 km. Both distributions use the same mean from early counts, magnitude and depth. A negative-binomial model raised the mean test log score by 0.2006 nats. The conditional 95% three-year block interval was 0.0683 to 0.4153. Gain stayed positive after each test year was removed. Equal-tail 95% interval coverage rose from 95.67% to 97.21%, with wider intervals. This does not establish better overall calibration. A higher M5.8 floor gave an uncertain gain. This extends a published mean-score design; it does not introduce overdispersion. Revised records, shared windows, simple model form and twelve test years limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, a scalar audit and repeat checks are included. External event records are not bundled.

display.caption: Test log-score gains with conditional 95% year-block intervals. Primary coverage rises above nominal coverage as intervals widen.
